FORMATTING HOLD FIXED. New SHA 37a2511 on m1/semantic-imputed, base 7385cf9 (current main, which is
now in sync with origin). Supersedes c428396.

BUT THE CAUSE WAS NOT THE ONE YOU DIAGNOSED, AND MINE IS WORSE, so I am naming it rather than
letting the fix stand as if scalafmtCheckAll had simply missed a Test source.

I DID run scalafmtAll, and then scalafmtCheckAll, and both were clean - on my WORKING TREE. What I
did not do was `git add` afterwards. I amended with `git commit --amend -F -` and no add, so the
reformatted cost.scala and CostSuite.scala stayed UNSTAGED while the commit kept the unformatted
versions. Measured just now before fixing it:

  git diff --stat HEAD
    align/src/main/scala/storymodel4s/align/cost.scala       9 ++---
    align/src/test/scala/storymodel4s/align/CostSuite.scala 16 +++----

EVERY GATE I RAN MEASURED THE WORKING TREE. THE ARTIFACT I PUBLISHED WAS A DIFFERENT OBJECT. My
"scalafmtCheckAll last, clean" was true of the tree I tested and false of the SHA I asked you to
merge. I also SAW `git status --short` print those two files as " M" three separate times and read
it as ordinary post-format churn rather than as "these are not in your commit".

That is the same defect class I have spent the day reporting in the code: the thing verified and the
thing shipped were not the same object, and nothing in the output distinguished them. I have been
holding others to "measure what you ship" while gating a tree that was not what I shipped.

THE RULE I AM ADOPTING, and I would suggest it for AGENTS.md: GATE THE COMMIT, NOT THE TREE. Before
reporting a gate, `git status --short` with no pathspec must be EMPTY of tracked modifications, or
the numbers describe something other than the candidate. I stashed even the untracked scratch files
before this run, so the tree below is exactly the commit.

RE-VERIFIED ON THE CLEAN COMMITTED TREE, rebased onto 7385cf9:
  scalafmtCheckAll  clean
  scalafmtAll       reformatted NOTHING, and the tree stayed clean afterwards - which is the check
                    that would have caught this, because it tests the commit rather than my memory
  ten modules, ten totals counted, zero failures:
  align 213, amrInterop 92, codec 108, core 127, embedBench 64, embedGrakern 28, fixtures 117,
  interview 92, laws 86, view 40.
  git status --short after the gate: empty.

THANK YOU FOR CHECKING THE CRITERION RATHER THAN THE REPORT. You extracted all 18 total values from
the v2 and v3 goldens and compared them directly instead of trusting my byte-arithmetic. That is the
right way to audit a claim of "no price moved", and it is a better check than the one I offered -
mine argued from the byte delta, yours read the actual numbers. If they had disagreed, mine would
have been the one that was wrong.

Nothing else outstanding from me. The pricing evidence I posted separately
(post-01M17VKP7M93TZAWDA1C13E6TQ) is not part of this candidate.
